**Cause:** `leaks()` in `src/leaks.py:8` runs the transcript through `json.dumps` before searching it. JSON escapes every backslash, so `C:\Users\dana` is stored as `C:\\Users\\dana` in the text being searched. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so it never matches. `/home/dana` has no characters that JSON escapes, so it matches.

I reproduced it without touching `src/`:

- Transcript with `dir C:\Users\dana`, secret `C:\Users\dana` → `[]` (missed)
- Transcript with `cat /home/dana/notes.txt`, secret `/home/dana` → `['/home/dana']` (caught)

The existing tests only cover the `/home/dana` form, which is why this went unnoticed. The fix belongs to the other session. It would need to search the raw strings in `target` and `output` instead of the JSON encoding, or add escaped variants of each secret. I haven't changed anything in the repo.
